newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - BRITISH BUSINESS PRESS - AUG 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - BRITISH BUSINESS PRESS - AUG 15.

DAILY TELEGRAPH -- APPLE STAFF LOSE PERKS AS EX-BOSSSES SELL $14M STAKE

New board member and co-founder of computer company Apple, Steve Jobs, announced that the company is having to tighten its belt, by diminishing staff perks, to regain the company's egalitarian and entrepreneurial roots. Staff have been informed that they will have to take economy class flights on most services and have a cut in severance pay and have share options instead of cash bonuses. The news comes as two former chairmen of the company are to sell their shares worth more than $14m. -- BOOTS DENIES $98M SETTLEMENT ROLE

Pharmacy group Boots has denied involvement in the $98m US law settlement of German drug company BASF, which was faced with a $8.5bn lawsuit for the alleged suppression of a report that said its thyroid treatment, Synthroid, was no more effective than cheaper generic drugs. Nearly 5m claimants are involved in the case concerning the drug which BASF took over from Boots two years ago, but although Boots was named in the lawsuit it has claimed it was not a 'proper defendant'.
-- DISNEY'S ABC CHANNEL CUTS JOBS AMID RATINGS FALL

Walt Disney-owned television company ABC has axed 200 jobs, as it prepares its annual budget for its parent company, following a recent down-turn in ratings which has seen the station slip its position from second to third, behind rivals NBC and CBS. ABC has about 5,000 employees and is reducing numbers apparently on its own initiative and not from direct Disney orders.
THE TIMES -- ORANGE DOUBLES SPENDING TO STAY AHEAD OF RIVALS

Mobile phone company Orange is planning to double investment in its network to 800m stg before the end of the decade. The plans are an attempt by Orange, the newest of the four UK mobile phone companies, to keep ahead of its rivals. The company is planning the construction of 3,100 additional transmission sites in order to improve the range and power of signal coverage.
-- ALBERT FISHER PLANS SALE AFTER SPURNING US BID

Food company Albert Fisher has rejected a takeover bid from Chiquita, the American banana supplier, and is set to put its seafood division up for sale. It is understood that Fisher was unhappy that much of the Chiquita offer was in shares rather than cash. Shares in Fisher, which has also issued a profits warning, fell 11 per cent on Thursday to 38.75p.
-- DRUG BLOW FOR XENOVA AS LOSS DEEPENS

Drug development company Xenova has reported an increase in pre-tax losses for the six months to June 30 of 5.9m stg, compared to 3.2m stg last time, as spending on research and development during the period rose to 6.3m stg. The company has suffered a setback in the development of its lead product, the cancer treatment XR5000, which has been giving side effect problems and is now unlikely to reach the market before 2001. THE GUARDIAN -- LINES CLEARED FOR C&W TO EXPAND IN AUSTRALIA

Australian Treasurer Peter Costello has said that it is no longer necessary for foreign ownership in Optus Commuications, the country's second-largest telecom and cable TV group, to be limited. The announcement clears the way for Cable and Wireless C&W.L of the UK to take control of the company it helped found in 1992. C&W can now double its stake in Optus to 49 per cent by buying Bell South's stake for 445m stg.
-- LAURA ASHLEY FACES CRISIS OF CONFIDENCE

Laura Ashley, the fashion and home furnishings group, is at the centre of City speculation that it is about to announce a halt to its American expansion and job losses at its Welsh factories. The company is due to issue an emergency trading statement next week, but some analysts have expressed concern that the company has allowed the speculation to grow by promising the statement three weeks ahead of its publication.
-- INQUIRY INTO TOMB RAIDER SHARES

Share dealings in Eidos, the company which developed the chart-topping computer game Tomb Raider, are understood to be under investigation by City regulators. The inquiry is thought to centre on dealings in Eidos shares by a number of off-shore companies ahead of price-sensitive news announcements, and it is believed that the allegations of impropriety extend to traders at two large investment banks.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- NORTHERN IRELAND WATCHDOG SET TO REFER GENERATORS TO MMC

Three electicity generating companies in Northern Ireland could face a referral to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission in a long-running dispute with the industry regulator in the province over power prices. The regulator, Douglas McIldoon, received a report of independent research into the 300m stg generation market earlier this week, and a referral to the MMC is thought to be likely.
-- FREEPAGES ON UPWARD TURN

AIM-listed telephone information service Freepages has appointed Cazenove as joint brokers of the company after reporting a reduction in losses in the third quarter of this year. The company reported a pre-tax loss of 2.38m stg for the third quarter to June, compared to a loss of 2.596m stg for the same period last year. The Cazenove appointment has been seen as a bid by Freepages to move away from controversies which have affected the company's share price, including the links between former chairman Ronald Zimet and the failed attempt by Andrew Regan to take over the Co-op.
-- WESTMINSTER TO SELL OFF 15 NURSING HOMES

Nursing home group Westminster Health Care, which reported strong annual results Thursday, is planning to sell off up to 15 of its 105 nursing homes over the next 18 months as part of move to refocus on faster-growing areas such as retirement centres and drug abuse clinics. The company reported a 14 per cent increase in pre-tax profits to 20m stg in the year to May, excluding 2.7m stg costs of last year's failed bid for Goldsborough and a one- off charge of 3.1m stg to reduce investment in the nursing home sector.
